papers.title: scChronos: Hierarchical Temporal Context Learning for Missing Snapshot Prediction in Single-Cell Time Series
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Single-cell time-series atlases provide discrete cross-sectional snapshots of continuous developmental processes, making missing-snapshot prediction essential for reconstructing trajectories and dynamic programs. However, destructive scRNA-seq profiling prevents tracking the same cells across time, yielding unpaired population snapshots and making missing-snapshot prediction challenging. Existing methods typically rely on explicit dynamical propagation or transport-based coupling between snapshots, which may ignore the statistical constraints of the overall population distribution and be sensitive to sampling noise and cell-to-cell variability. Results We introduce scChronos, a hierarchical temporal context learning framework that formulates missing-snapshot prediction as target-conditioned population distribution prediction rather than individual-cell propagation. Unlike cell-centric propagation approaches, scChronos explicitly captures dual-level dynamics: (i) Within each observed snapshot, scChronos compresses cell populations into cluster-representative cell representations with a transcriptomic encoder, preserving population information while reducing noise; (ii) Across reference snapshots, the dual-branch temporal context integration module fuses information from all available and nearby time points into a temporal representation, which is then decoded with learnable cell-generation seeds to predict the target distribution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that scChronos improves both interpolation-style recovery and extrapolation-style forecasting compared with state-of-the-art methods. Beyond reducing distributional discrepancy, scChronos better preserves developmental topology and maintains cell-type-specific marker and pathway programs. Availability The code and data are available at https://github.com/yjs193/scChronos and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20933283

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
单细胞时间序列图谱为连续的发育过程提供了离散的横截面快照，因此对于缺失快照的数据进行预测对于重建细胞的发育轨迹及动态变化规律至关重要。然而，破坏性的scRNA-seq分析方法使得无法追踪同一细胞在不同时间点的状态，从而导致获得的样本数据缺乏配对性，进而使缺失快照的预测变得极为困难。现有的方法通常依赖于显式的动态传播机制或基于细胞迁移的耦合模型，但这些方法可能会忽略整体细胞群体分布的统计特性，并且容易受到采样噪声及细胞间变异性的影响。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了scChronos这一分层式时间序列分析框架，它将缺失快照的预测问题转化为以目标状态为条件的细胞群体分布预测任务，而非针对单个细胞的动态追踪过程。与以往以细胞为中心的分析方法不同，scChronos能够同时捕捉两个层面的动态变化：  
(1) 在每个观测到的快照中，该框架利用转录组分析技术将细胞群体压缩成具有代表性的簇结构，从而在保留细胞群体信息的同时有效减少噪声；  
(2) 在不同时间点的快照之间，该框架通过双分支的时间序列整合模块，将所有可用数据及邻近时间点的信息融合成一个统一的时间序列表示，随后利用可学习的细胞生成模型来预测目标状态下的细胞分布。  

大量实验结果表明，与现有的最先进方法相比，scChronos在无论是进行插值式的数据恢复还是外推式的预测分析时，均表现出更优异的性能。除了能够有效减少数据分布的偏差外，该框架还能更好地保留细胞的发育拓扑结构，并保持不同细胞类型所特有的标记基因及信号通路特征。  

**代码与数据获取方式**

https://github.com/yjs193/scChronos  
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20933283

papers.title: CRISPR-HAWK: Haplotype- and Variant-Aware Guide Design Toolkit for CRISPR-Cas
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Current CRISPR guide RNA design tools rely on reference genomes, overlooking how genetic variation impacts editing outcomes. As genome editing advances toward clinical applications, incorporating population diversity becomes essential for ensuring therapeutic efficacy across diverse populations. Results We present CRISPR-HAWK, a framework integrating individual- and population-scale variants and haplotypes into gRNA design. Analyzing therapeutic targets across 79,648 genomes reveals that genetic variants substantially alter guide performance. For the clinically approved sickle cell disease therapeutic guide targeting BCL11A, we identify haplotypes that completely abolish predicted cutting activity. Across seven therapeutic loci, 82.5% of guides contain variants modifying on-target activity. Variants also create novel protospacer adjacent motif sites generating individual-specific guides invisible to reference-based design. These findings demonstrate that variant-aware selection is critical for equitable genome editing. Availability CRISPR-HAWK is available at https://github.com/pinellolab/CRISPR-HAWK and https://github.com/InfOmics/CRISPR-HAWK

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
目前的CRISPR引导RNA设计工具主要依赖于参考基因组，但这些工具并未考虑遗传变异对编辑效果的影响。随着基因组编辑技术向临床应用迈进，将群体多样性纳入设计流程对于确保不同人群的治疗效果至关重要。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了CRISPR-HAWK这一框架，该框架将个体及群体层面的遗传变异与单倍型信息整合到引导RNA的设计过程中。通过对79,648个基因组中的治疗靶点进行分析，我们发现遗传变异会显著影响引导RNA的编辑效果。以已被临床批准的针对BCL11A基因的镰状细胞病治疗用引导RNA为例，我们发现了某些能够完全消除其切割活性的单倍型；在7个治疗位点中，有82.5%的引导RNA含有会改变其靶向效果的遗传变异。此外，这些变异还会生成新的序列结构，从而产生针对特定个体的、无法通过基于参考基因组的设计方法生成的引导RNA。这些研究结果表明，在进行基因组编辑时，必须充分考虑遗传变异的影响，才能确保治疗的公平性。

all_papers.title: scChronos: Hierarchical Temporal Context Learning for Missing Snapshot Prediction in Single-Cell Time Series
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Single-cell time-series atlases provide discrete cross-sectional snapshots of continuous developmental processes, making missing-snapshot prediction essential for reconstructing trajectories and dynamic programs. However, destructive scRNA-seq profiling prevents tracking the same cells across time, yielding unpaired population snapshots and making missing-snapshot prediction challenging. Existing methods typically rely on explicit dynamical propagation or transport-based coupling between snapshots, which may ignore the statistical constraints of the overall population distribution and be sensitive to sampling noise and cell-to-cell variability. Results We introduce scChronos, a hierarchical temporal context learning framework that formulates missing-snapshot prediction as target-conditioned population distribution prediction rather than individual-cell propagation. Unlike cell-centric propagation approaches, scChronos explicitly captures dual-level dynamics: (i) Within each observed snapshot, scChronos compresses cell populations into cluster-representative cell representations with a transcriptomic encoder, preserving population information while reducing noise; (ii) Across reference snapshots, the dual-branch temporal context integration module fuses information from all available and nearby time points into a temporal representation, which is then decoded with learnable cell-generation seeds to predict the target distribution. Extensive experiments demonstrate that scChronos improves both interpolation-style recovery and extrapolation-style forecasting compared with state-of-the-art methods. Beyond reducing distributional discrepancy, scChronos better preserves developmental topology and maintains cell-type-specific marker and pathway programs. Availability The code and data are available at https://github.com/yjs193/scChronos and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20933283

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
单细胞时间序列图谱为连续的发育过程提供了离散的横截面快照，因此对于缺失快照的数据进行预测对于重建细胞的发育轨迹及动态变化规律至关重要。然而，破坏性的scRNA-seq分析方法使得无法追踪同一细胞在不同时间点的状态，从而导致获得的样本数据缺乏配对性，进而使缺失快照的预测变得极为困难。现有的方法通常依赖于显式的动态传播机制或基于细胞迁移的耦合模型，但这些方法可能会忽略整体细胞群体分布的统计特性，并且容易受到采样噪声及细胞间变异性的影响。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了scChronos这一分层式时间序列分析框架，它将缺失快照的预测问题转化为以目标状态为条件的细胞群体分布预测任务，而非针对单个细胞的动态追踪过程。与以往以细胞为中心的分析方法不同，scChronos能够同时捕捉两个层面的动态变化：  
(1) 在每个观测到的快照中，该框架利用转录组分析技术将细胞群体压缩成具有代表性的簇结构，从而在保留细胞群体信息的同时有效减少噪声；  
(2) 在不同时间点的快照之间，该框架通过双分支的时间序列整合模块，将所有可用数据及邻近时间点的信息融合成一个统一的时间序列表示，随后利用可学习的细胞生成模型来预测目标状态下的细胞分布。  

大量实验结果表明，与现有的最先进方法相比，scChronos在无论是进行插值式的数据恢复还是外推式的预测分析时，均表现出更优异的性能。除了能够有效减少数据分布的偏差外，该框架还能更好地保留细胞的发育拓扑结构，并保持不同细胞类型所特有的标记基因及信号通路特征。  

**代码与数据获取方式**

all_papers.title: CRISPR-HAWK: Haplotype- and Variant-Aware Guide Design Toolkit for CRISPR-Cas
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Current CRISPR guide RNA design tools rely on reference genomes, overlooking how genetic variation impacts editing outcomes. As genome editing advances toward clinical applications, incorporating population diversity becomes essential for ensuring therapeutic efficacy across diverse populations. Results We present CRISPR-HAWK, a framework integrating individual- and population-scale variants and haplotypes into gRNA design. Analyzing therapeutic targets across 79,648 genomes reveals that genetic variants substantially alter guide performance. For the clinically approved sickle cell disease therapeutic guide targeting BCL11A, we identify haplotypes that completely abolish predicted cutting activity. Across seven therapeutic loci, 82.5% of guides contain variants modifying on-target activity. Variants also create novel protospacer adjacent motif sites generating individual-specific guides invisible to reference-based design. These findings demonstrate that variant-aware selection is critical for equitable genome editing. Availability CRISPR-HAWK is available at https://github.com/pinellolab/CRISPR-HAWK and https://github.com/InfOmics/CRISPR-HAWK

摘要：动机  
目前，用于设计CRISPR引导RNA的工具均依赖于参考基因组，而这些工具忽略了遗传变异对编辑结果的影响。
llm_highlights_zh: 随着基因组编辑技术向临床应用迈进，在实际应用中纳入人群的遗传多样性对于确保不同人群都能从中获得治疗效果至关重要。

通过对79,648个基因组进行分析，研究发现：遗传变异会显著影响相关治疗靶点的效果。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
目前的CRISPR引导RNA设计工具主要依赖于参考基因组，但这些工具并未考虑遗传变异对编辑效果的影响。随着基因组编辑技术向临床应用迈进，将群体多样性纳入设计流程对于确保不同人群的治疗效果至关重要。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了CRISPR-HAWK这一框架，该框架将个体及群体层面的遗传变异与单倍型信息整合到引导RNA的设计过程中。通过对79,648个基因组中的治疗靶点进行分析，我们发现遗传变异会显著影响引导RNA的编辑效果。以已被临床批准的针对BCL11A基因的镰状细胞病治疗用引导RNA为例，我们发现了某些能够完全消除其切割活性的单倍型；在7个治疗位点中，有82.5%的引导RNA含有会改变其靶向效果的遗传变异。此外，这些变异还会生成新的序列结构，从而产生针对特定个体的、无法通过基于参考基因组的设计方法生成的引导RNA。这些研究结果表明，在进行基因组编辑时，必须充分考虑遗传变异的影响，才能确保治疗的公平性。  

**获取方式**  
CRISPR-HAWK工具已发布在以下链接中：  
https://github.com/pinellolab/CRISPR-HAWK  
https://github.com/InfOmics/CRISPR-HAWK
